mothbeans.tips: Extremely drought tolerant — ideal for arid and semi-arid regions of Rajasthan and Gujarat. Sow at 30x10 cm spacing with 8–10 kg seed per hectare. Requires no irrigation if monsoon is adequate. Harvest pods when 80% turn brown. Excellent for improving soil fertility.

rice.tips: Transplant seedlings after 25–30 days in nursery. Maintain 5 cm standing water during tillering stage. Apply urea in three split doses for better nitrogen uptake.

maize.tips: Sow seeds at 4–5 cm depth with 60x20 cm spacing. Apply NPK 120:60:40 kg/ha. Ensure good drainage — maize cannot tolerate waterlogging. Harvest when husks turn brown.

chickpea.tips: Sow after first winter rain when soil temperature drops below 25°C. Do not apply excess nitrogen — chickpea fixes its own through root nodules. Spray for pod borer at flowering stage.

kidneybeans.tips: Requires well-drained fertile soil. Inoculate seeds with Rhizobium before sowing. Avoid waterlogging — provide raised beds in heavy rainfall areas. Harvest pods when they dry on plant.

pigeonpeas.tips: Inter-crop with soybean or sorghum for better land use. Requires long duration (150–180 days) — plan field accordingly. Spray monocrotophos for pod fly control at pod-filling stage.

mungbean.tips: Short duration crop (60–75 days) — excellent for crop rotation. Sow 20–25 kg seeds per hectare. Spray Chlorpyrifos for thrips control. Harvest in 2–3 pickings as pods mature.

blackgram.tips: Highly suitable after paddy harvest in Rabi season. Does not require much fertilizer — apply only phosphorus at sowing. Harvest when 70–80% pods turn black.

lentil.tips: Grows well on residual moisture from Kharif — saves irrigation cost. Sow at 4–5 cm depth. Apply one light irrigation at pod formation. Harvest before pods shatter.

pomegranate.tips: Use drip irrigation for best results — pomegranate is highly drought tolerant once established. Practice 'Hasta Bahar' (October cropping) for premium quality fruit. Prune dead wood after each harvest. Spray Bordeaux mixture to prevent fungal diseases.

banana.tips: Plant tissue culture suckers for disease-free crop. Maintain 1.8x1.5 m spacing. Apply 200 g urea + 150 g MOP per plant every month. Provide windbreaks to protect from storm damage. Harvest when 75% mature.

mango.tips: Grafted varieties give early bearing (3–4 years). Spray Paclobutrazol in October for flower induction. Stop irrigation before flowering to avoid vegetative growth. Harvest at 'physiological maturity' for export quality.

grapes.season: Pruning in Oct; Harvest in March–April
grapes.tips: Prune canes to 2–3 buds in October (back pruning). Apply Gibberellic Acid spray for better berry size. Drip irrigation is essential — 4–8 liters/vine/day. Harvest early morning to preserve sugar content.

watermelon.tips: Grows best in sandy loam soil. Sow in raised beds. Limit irrigation during ripening for sweeter fruit. Tap the fruit — hollow sound means it is ripe. One vine can yield 4–6 fruits.

muskmelon.tips: Requires hot and dry climate during fruit ripening. Mulch the beds to conserve moisture. Stop irrigation 10 days before harvest for better aroma and sugar. Do not apply too much nitrogen — leads to poor taste.

apple.tips: Requires chilling hours (1000–1500 hours below 7°C) — suitable only in hills. Plant high-density orchards (1250 trees/ha) for early and higher yield. Thin fruits at marble size for large-sized apples. Spray micronutrients (Boron, Zinc) for better color.

orange.tips: Nagpur mandarin is India's most popular variety. Apply Ammonium sulphate instead of urea for better fruit quality. Avoid waterlogging — use raised beds. Spray urea 1% at fruit setting stage for higher yield.

papaya.tips: Plant 'Red Lady' hybrid variety for high yield. Space at 1.8x1.8 m. Apply fertilizer every 2 months. Support plants with bamboo stakes in windy areas. Harvest when skin shows yellow tinge. Rich returns in less than a year.

coconut.tips: Plant 'Chowghat Orange Dwarf' or 'West Coast Tall' varieties. Apply 50 kg cow dung + 1.3 kg urea per tree annually. Drip irrigation at 40 liters/tree/day gives 50% more yield. Harvest every 45 days. Inter-crop cocoa or vanilla for extra income.

cotton.tips: Use Bt cotton hybrid varieties for bollworm resistance. Avoid dense sowing — maintain 90x60 cm spacing. Spray NPK 19:19:19 at boll formation stage. Pick cotton in the morning when moisture is low. Avoid irrigation at flowering stage.

jute.tips: Grows best in humid Bengal-type climate. Broadcast 5–7 kg seeds per hectare. Thin seedlings at 10 cm height. Ret (soak) harvested stalks in clean water for 15–20 days to separate fibres. Used for eco-friendly bags and packaging.

coffee.tips: Grow under shade trees (Silver Oak) for best quality beans. Apply 40 g Zinc Sulphate per plant annually. Pulp the red cherries within 12 hours of harvest. 'Robusta' variety is hardier; 'Arabica' gives premium price. Grown mainly in Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu hills.
